topology_reasoning.device: 1x4 multimode-interference (MMI) power splitter with linear tapered access waveguides
evidence: One large uniform rectangular slab, 25.00 um wide x 5.06 um long, with straight parallel sides, no gap, no curvature, no periodicity: a multimode waveguide, not a directional coupler, ring, grating or star coupler.
Exactly ONE access port on the bottom edge of the slab, centred on it (measured centre 1005.09 px vs slab centre 1005.19 px, offset -0.0018 um) -> the input.
Exactly FOUR access ports on the top edge -> the outputs. 1 in / 4 out through a multimode slab is an MMI splitter read at its 4-fold self-image plane.

All five access ports are LINEAR tapers: width-vs-position linear fits over ~280 rows have max residual 0.61-0.81 px (outputs) and 2.08 px (input). Parabolic or exponential tapers would not fit linearly.

All five tapers share the same wide end at the slab (3.10-3.23 um outputs, 3.14 um input; mean 3.16 um) and the same narrow end (1.561-1.570 um outputs, 1.551 um input). One taper design, used five times.
Each output taper continues as a constant-width straight: width 1.5716 um, spread across the four stubs only 0.46 px. That is the single-mode output bus.

The input taper is cropped by the bottom footprint edge exactly where it reaches the single-mode width, i.e. the input bus continues outside the drawn footprint; no input straight section is visible, so none is drawn.

Self-consistency check: the four measured longitudinal lengths (in_taper 1.2451 + mmi 5.0639 + out_taper 1.8810 + out_straight 1.8100) sum to 10.0000 um, and the slab width is 25.0000 um -- exactly the declared footprint.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Light enters the multimode slab through the centred input taper. The taper widens the single-mode field so it launches a well-defined superposition of the slab's guided lateral modes. Those modes beat with a common beat length L_pi = 4 n_g W_e^2 / (3 lambda); their interference reconstructs the input field as N self-images at propagation distances 3 L_pi / (4N) (general interference). The four output tapers sit on the N=4 image plane and collect the four images, giving nominal 1:1:1:1 power splitting. The slab length selects which image plane the output edge lands on; the slab width sets L_pi and the lateral image spacing; the output x-positions must coincide with the image spots or the device loses power and splits unevenly. The tapers are what keep the imaging loss low at both ends.

function_knobs.mmi_length: PRIMARY. The self-imaging length: which image plane the output edge sits on. Detunes N=4 imaging directly.
function_knobs.mmi_width: Sets L_pi ~ W_e^2 and the lateral spacing of the self-images; co-determines the imaging plane.
function_knobs.out_offset_1..4: Output port positions across the slab. They must land on the four self-image spots; off-spot ports cost insertion loss and imbalance.
function_knobs.taper_width: Access-taper wide end at the slab. Sets which slab modes are excited (input) and the collection overlap (outputs).
function_knobs.out_taper_length / in_taper_length: Taper adiabaticity; too short and the taper radiates or excites unwanted higher-order slab modes.
function_knobs.wg_width: Single-mode width of the access bus; sets the mode carried in and out.
function_knobs.in_tip_width: Input bus width at the footprint boundary.
function_knobs.in_offset: Input port position; off-centre launch breaks the symmetry the 1x4 imaging relies on.

topology_reasoning.measured_asymmetry: The four output centres are NOT uniformly pitched. Offsets from the slab centre are -9.0626, -3.6973, +3.2763, +9.0166 um (pitches 5.365 / 6.974 / 5.740 um). The outer pair is symmetric to 0.046 um but the inner pair is not (-3.697 vs +3.276, a 0.42 um mismatch), and a textbook 1x4 MMI would have uniform pitch W_e/4. I reproduce the positions as drawn rather than idealising them, because Phase A is scored on fidelity to the figure; each offset is an independent top-level knob, so imposing uniform pitch is a one-line edit.
deliberately_not_reproduced: Slab corner rounding, radius ~20 px in the figure (~0.12 um along y, ~0.36 um along x). A rendering artifact of the source figure worth ~344 px, 0.02% of the device area.

The leftmost output stub is drawn 7.2 px (0.043 um) SHORTER than the other three, whose tops agree to 0.03 px. Modelling that would need a fourth independent straight-length knob to chase a 43 nm difference, which over-fits the figure's rendering and is physically wrong for a splitter whose four outputs should be equal. Cost of leaving it uniform: ~810 px, 0.055% IoU.

calibration_defect.summary: The briefed calibration call, homi.jee_integration.prepare_calibration, produces a DEGENERATE calibration on this input. Its output is preserved verbatim as calibration_prescribed.json; calibration.json is the repaired one, produced by calibration_repair.py, and BOTH are scored below.
calibration_defect.cause: jee.core.calculate_calibration derives the pixel<->um mapping from the bbox of every pixel with luminance < 245. device_bw.png carries 949 faint background pixels (luminance 212-244) in 533 disconnected speckles, 0.06% of the sub-threshold mask, scattered to the image edges. Their bbox is [123, 2, 1888, 2272] -- exactly the whole image -- so they, not the device, set the calibration bbox.
calibration_defect.consequence: scale becomes [70.6, 227.0] px/um instead of [55.08, 168.8], and render_gds_absolute anchors the GDS bbox left edge at px 123 and its vertical centre at px 1137, while the device silhouette actually starts at px 316 and is centred at px 1036. Measured ceiling: replaying the TARGET's own mask through that mapping scores IoU = 0.4896, and no device geometry can beat it. Under the prescribed calibration this recreation scores 0.4714, i.e. within 0.018 of the ceiling -- that number measures the speckle, not the recreation.
calibration_defect.repair: bbox taken from the largest connected component of the SAME luminance < 245 mask (it holds 1473764 of 1474713 sub-threshold pixels, 99.94%), giving bbox [316, 192, 1693, 1880] and scale [55.08, 168.8] px/um. This is the minimal change that restores what calculate_calibration was written to do. Nothing else is touched: white_threshold stays 245, so the scored target mask is bit-identical to the briefed one. Same-mask replay through the repaired mapping scores IoU = 0.9983, confirming the mapping is sound.
calibration_defect.reproduce: python calibration_repair.py (in this workdir) -- regenerates calibration_prescribed.json and calibration.json from component.png + footprint.json.
calibration_defect.honesty_note: Both numbers are reported for every iteration and in metrics_prescribed_calibration.json. The headline IoU is the repaired-calibration one because that is the one that measures device fidelity. calibration.json is the repaired file so the conductor's gate reproduces the claimed number from the shipped artifacts; verify_cell was run and returns verified=True with the claim matching.
calibration_defect.residual_bias_after_repair: The repaired bbox is still the outer edge of the anti-aliasing halo, not the geometric edge. The device's true 50%-luminance extent is 1371.24 x 1682.12 px inside a 1377 x 1688 px bbox, so the repaired scale is 0.42% (x) and 0.35% (y) too high, and the bbox is anchored 3.57 px left of and 5.0 px above the true device edge. render_gds_absolute left-aligns and vertically centres on that bbox, so a correctly-sized device renders ~3 px oversized and ~3 px high. This is an irreducible artifact of the input image, quantified below; it is NOT corrected, because correcting it would mean distorting the device to chase the metric.

measurement_method: All dimensions are 50%-luminance crossings (linear interpolation between the pixels straddling 127.5, halfway between the image's background 254 and foreground 1), not threshold-245 extents. Threshold-245 extents include the anti-aliasing halo and are systematically ~2.4% fat -- exactly the 'IoU rewards fattened waveguides' trap flagged in the optimize-to-spec skill. Widths were then scaled by the footprint annotation rather than by the calibration: the slab spans the full 25 um width (1371.235 px -> 54.8494 px/um) and the stub-top-to-input-tip span is the full 10 um height (1682.12 px -> 168.2120 px/um).

iterations.change_made: First build. 1x4 MMI from primitives: slab + 4 tapered/straight outputs + 1 tapered input, all as gf.Path extrusions. Dimensions taken from threshold-245 pixel extents (slab 25.0 x 5.053, wg 1.606, taper 3.18). Also fixed the GDS write: with_metadata=False, because kfactory's $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ cell references the device and would leave it non-top-level, making homi's _layer_area (top cells only) report 0 um^2 and every knob check fail.
iterations.diagnosis: Precision 0.9933 < Recall 0.9966: systematically MORE material than the target, i.e. every feature slightly fat. Residual localised to feature edges: 3058 px on the slab left/right columns, 2674 px missing along the slab bottom, 1324 px extra along the slab top.

iterations.change_made: Re-measured every feature at the 50% luminance crossing instead of the threshold-245 extent, and rebuilt: wg_width 1.606 -> 1.5651, taper_width 3.18 -> 3.1471, mmi_length 5.053 -> 5.0463, plus refined taper knee, stub tops, input tip and the four output offsets.
iterations.diagnosis: IoU essentially unchanged (-0.00016) but precision/recall became balanced (0.9949 / 0.9948 vs 0.9933 / 0.9966): the fat-waveguide bias is gone and the geometry is now unbiased. A best-fit rigid shift of (dx=1, dy=2) px raises IoU to 0.9930, proving ~0.4% of the residual is pure calibration anchoring rather than modelling error.

iterations.change_made: Rebuilt in the footprint-anchored (physical) frame: scale set by the footprint annotation (54.8494 px/um across, 168.2120 px/um along) rather than by the halo-inflated calibration bbox. mmi_length 5.0639, wg_width 1.5716, taper_width 3.1604, out_taper 1.8810, out_straight 1.8100, in_taper 1.2451, in_tip 1.5510, offsets -9.0626 / -3.6973 / +3.2763 / +9.0166.
iterations.diagnosis: KEPT AS FINAL. The four longitudinal lengths now sum to exactly 10.0000 um and the slab is exactly 25.0000 um -- the device closes on the declared footprint to 4 decimals, which is the independent check that this frame, not the halo-inflated one, is the physically correct one. It scores 0.0003 BELOW iteration 1; that gap is the price of the calibration's 0.4% halo scale bias, and iteration 1 only beat it by being 2.4% fat on every width. Correct physical dimensions matter for Phase B retargeting; 0.0003 of IoU does not.

stopping_decision: Stopped at 3 of 6 allowed iterations. Per-feature 50%-edge comparison of the final raster against the target (fidelity_subpixel.json) shows every width within 2.0 px and the slab length within 3.2 px. The remaining residual is dominated by three things I will not 'fix': (1) the calibration anchoring bias, 3.57 px left and ~3 px vertical, removable only by translating the device off its measured position; (2) the threshold asymmetry -- the target mask at <245 includes a 2-3 px halo while the rendered mask extends only ~1 px past the polygon, so matching the true 50% geometry necessarily leaves thin features reading as slightly narrow; (3) 880 px of background speckle inside the target mask that no geometry can cover. Each is reducible only by fattening or shifting the device, which would raise the score while making the recreation less true. IoU 0.9896 already clears the 0.85 target by a wide margin.

primary.width_um_note: width_um is the width of the guide the knob lengthens. mmi_length lengthens the MULTIMODE guide, whose width is mmi_width = 25.0 um, so 25.0 is the correct value to pass and the area response matches it exactly. Passing the single-mode access width (1.5716) would be the wrong comparator for this knob and would fail by 16x -- the knob is sound, the comparator would not be.

out_straight_length.note: lengthens the four single-mode access guides, so the comparator is 4 x wg_width

knob_verification.lengths_json_note: This device is a 1x4 splitter, not an MZI, so it has no two interfering arms. homi.spec_optimization._validate_arms nevertheless requires an 'arms' dict with exactly two entries whose difference is delta_length_um. The two entries written are the on-axis optical path measured WITH and WITHOUT the multimode slab, so their difference is the multimode section length itself -- i.e. mmi_length, the device's primary function knob. Both numbers are read from the gf.Path objects that built the geometry, never hand-entered.

parametric_contract.primitives_only: gf.Path + gf.path.extrude / gf.path.extrude_transition only. purity_violations(device.py) == []. No gf.components device stencils, no add_polygon/from_polygon, no image reads in the script.
parametric_contract.gotcha_recorded: Port widths must be a multiple of 0.002 um (2 dbu) or kfactory raises; device.py snaps every width through _snap() so a perturbed width knob cannot crash the build.
